commands.review_summary:
Adds a `bird whoami` fallback to `import hydrate-profiles` that parses display names, updates `acct_primary` and `profile_me` in local mode, clears stale ids/avatars on identity changes, and adds focused tests.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main returns with `hydratedAccount: false` whenever the transport is not `xurl`, so bird-authenticated local mode cannot correct the seeded account. I did not run a live bird setup in this read-only review.

target.title: fix: hydrate local account identity from bird transport
target.body:
## Problem

The web UI showed the seeded `@steipete` placeholder — handle, display name, **and avatar** — whenever the **bird** transport was active. `hydrateProfilesFromX` only ran under the `xurl` transport and bailed out early in local/bird mode, so the seeded default account was never corrected to the authenticated user.

## Changes

- Correct `acct_primary` + `profile_me` from `bird whoami` (handle, name, `external_user_id`) when xurl is unavailable but bird is authenticated.
- Parse the display name that bird prints as `@handle (Display Name)`.
- Treat a **changed handle as an identity change even when `bird whoami` omits a numeric id** (`BirdAuthenticatedAccount.id` is optional). On any identity change, reset `external_user_id` (instead of coalescing) and clear the seeded `avatar_url` so no field from the prior account lingers on the new handle. The UI then falls back to initials — bird whoami cannot supply an avatar.

## Usage

Hydration stays an explicit, idempotent command (no new startup side effects):

```bash
birdclaw import hydrate-profiles   # after init, or after switching bird accounts
```

## Real behavior proof

Against a real bird-authenticated setup (ids redacted), in a throwaway `BIRDCLAW_HOME`:

```
$ bird whoami
📍 Safari
🙋 @martintrojer (Martin Trojer)
🪪 <user-id>
⚙️ graphql

$ birdclaw init          # seeds the @steipete placeholder
# BEFORE hydrate:
#   accounts: handle=@steipete  name=Peter  external_user_id=25401953
#   profiles: avatar=https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1131851609774985216/OcsssQ9J.png  (steipete's real photo)

$ birdclaw import hydrate-profiles
{ ok: true, hydratedProfiles: 0, hydratedAccount: true,
  reason: 'xurl not installed. local mode active.' }

# AFTER hydrate:
#   accounts: handle=@martintrojer  name=Martin Trojer  external_user_id=<user-id>
#   profiles: avatar=NULL   (falls back to initials, no longer the wrong photo)
```

## Notes / open questions

- I intentionally did **not** wire this into `birdclaw serve` startup to avoid running a `bird whoami` subprocess on every server boot. Happy to add an opt-in hook if you'd prefer the UI to self-correct.

## Test Plan

Ran tests — `bird.test.ts` + `profile-hydration.test.ts`, 39 passing (includes coverage for the idless changed-handle path and for preserving the id/avatar when the handle is unchanged).
